 DSWD pays over P31 million to drought-hit farmers in Capalonga, Paracale
 More than P31 million in emergency cash has reached drought-hit farmers in Capalonga and Paracale, and DSWD says payouts in other Camarines Norte towns are scheduled this week. #DSWD #ElNiño #CamarinesNorte #drought #farmers
 by 
 ASTIG PR 
 2 days ago 2 days ago 
 Advertisements 
 Two drought-hit towns in Camarines Norte have received more than P31 million in emergency cash from the Department of Social Welfare and Development, and the agency says more towns in the province are next in line this week.
 The payouts in Capalonga and Paracale are the agency’s latest round of emergency cash transfers for farmers whose crops were destroyed by a drought that could stretch into early next year. DSWD Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao gave the figures in a radio interview on Sunday.
 Where the money went
 Town 
 Amount 
 Beneficiaries 
 Payout dates

 P20,653,500

 Paracale 
 P10,521,000

 DSWD Bicol released the Capalonga tranche to 1,967 beneficiaries over two days, then paid 1,002 farmers in Paracale on Friday. Both releases went through the agency’s Field Office V.
 Why farmers are getting cash
 Dumlao said some farmers had already stopped planting because they feared another lost harvest would wipe out whatever they spent on seeds and labor. Farmers identified by local governments as the most severely affected by the drought are being prioritized for the cash aid.
 More than 191,000 families across six regions have been affected by El Niño, which could persist until early next year. The regions are Cagayan Valley, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Bicol, SOCCSKSARGEN and Caraga.
 In Region 2 alone, the DSWD has provided more than P141 million to corn and rice farmers in Isabela and Cagayan, made up of emergency cash transfers and family food packs. Nationwide, the agency said it had distributed more than P189 million in humanitarian assistance as of Nov. 7.
 The drought has already shown up in the national farm numbers. Farm output fell 5 percent in the third quarter as the rice harvest dropped 17.8 percent, and the weather bureau has warned that 68 provinces could be in drought by February .
 What comes next
 Other areas of Camarines Norte are scheduled to receive emergency cash transfers of P10,000 each this week and next week, Dumlao said. She added that the national total is expected to rise because more field reports are still coming in. 
 Her agency is also working against a thinning buffer of rice. Rice stocks fell 8.3 percent in a year while the NFA’s buffer dropped 38 percent .
 The Department of Agriculture has said it will coordinate with the Department of Labor and Employment to give El Niño-hit farmers temporary work through the TUPAD program while the dry spell lasts.
 (Photo: Presidential Communications Office via Wikimedia Commons, public domain. The image shows a DSWD relief distribution for families affected by the June 2026 Mindanao earthquake and does not depict the Camarines Norte payouts.)
